- When sentiment turns negative or shows strong bearish signals (e.g., -1.00 or 0.00), reduce forecasted price by 2–5% to account for downward momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% above recent mean), model tends to overreact — cap forecast peak at 10–15% above the immediate prior high.  
- If sentiment is consistently bullish (e.g., 1.00 across 5+ days), model often overestimates near-term upside — apply a 3–7% downward adjustment to avoid overfitting.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizons — if forecast is >10% above 14-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.  
- In 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates late-period volatility — add 1–3% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or bullish.  
- If sentiment shows “mixed” (e.g., 0.50 or 0.67) or recent volatility spikes, increase forecast variance by 10–20% to reflect uncertainty.
